entries.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
entries.snippet: Nvidia's share price have fallen 7% as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.

entries.title: French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial
entries.snippet: It is the latest case involving Nicolas Sarkozy who became the first French ex-president to go to jail last year.

entries.title: Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
entries.snippet: Saurav Das says immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him his passport had been flagged.

entries.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
entries.snippet: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.

entries.title: Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
entries.snippet: Nearly 1,000 children are among those killed or injured by explosives left over from the conflict, figures show.

entries.title: Nigerian monarch, 92, suspended after sexual assault claims
entries.snippet: The Emir of Daura is one of Nigeria's best-known monarchs, with politicians often trying to gain his support.

entries.title: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
entries.snippet: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.

entries.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
entries.snippet: German media said Russia planned to launch a satellite with a nuclear warhead into space in coming weeks.

entries.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
entries.snippet: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

entries.title: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
entries.snippet: Published extracts from the late pontiff's diary claim one of the visions happened "in the choir loft" during Mass.

entries.title: Gisèle Pelicot 'humiliated' after nude photos sent to media to promote book
entries.snippet: The publisher of an essay on coercive control apologises for "an unfortunate and inappropriate communication".

entries.title: Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
entries.snippet: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.

entries.title: Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20
entries.snippet: The explosion is the latest in a string of attacks on buildings housing the security forces and government offices.

entries.title: DR Congo says military aircraft missing as rebels claim to shoot down plane
entries.snippet: A South African fighter pilot and a Ugandan officer are reportedly among those aboard the downed plane.

entries.title: Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader
entries.snippet: Andrei Chibis, head of Russia's northern Murmansk region, is the first governor to be detained for five years.

entries.title: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
entries.snippet: Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were reportedly given 74 lashes in Qom.

entries.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
entries.snippet: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.

entries.title: Comedian impersonates Trump's dance moves, mocks trade talks at Canada press dinner
entries.snippet: The impersonator, Canadian comedian Mark Critch, poked fun at the US president's search for a new press secretary and US-Canada trade talks.

entries.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
entries.snippet: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.

entries.title: Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord
entries.snippet: Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops detained 'El Chapo Isidro', who had managed to evade capture for years.

entries.title: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
entries.snippet: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.

entries.title: The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
entries.snippet: The attacks, if officials who spoke to NPR are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the war with the U.S.

entries.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
entries.snippet: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

entries.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct
entries.snippet: President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

entries.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
entries.snippet: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

entries.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
entries.snippet: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

entries.title: They attended Trump's meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
entries.snippet: Trump's meme coin dinners have sparked intense controversy. These two guests attended his latest on Sunday — and agreed to provide NPR inside access.

entries.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
entries.snippet: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.

entries.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
entries.snippet: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

entries.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
entries.snippet: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.

entries.title: How Trump may have profited from Huang's return to Nvidia
entries.snippet: A day after President Trump intervened to reinstate Nvidia's embattled CEO, a new report suggests that Trump himself may have benefited financially to the tune of millions of dollars. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

entries.snippet: The U.S. Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate a highly volatile explosive compound in Iowa. The lead azide is used in military munitions and has been deteriorating underground. The detonation could send a plume of toxic lead dust across the area, but Army officials insist

entries.snippet: Hundreds of thousands of immigrants living legally in the U.S. recently lost their Medicaid coverage under a provision of President Trump's signature tax and spending law. The law is projected to reduce federal Medicaid spending by $900 billion over the next decade. Deema Zein re

entries.title: Bob Woodward reveals why he's naming sources in new book 'Secrets'

entries.title: 'Deals Drama Drive' traces how the Mondavi family helped spark Napa Valley's wine boom
entries.snippet: In 1966, Robert Mondavi and his son Michael opened Robert Mondavi Winery in California's Napa Valley. There, father and son helped spark a revolution and transform the region into one of the world's premier winemaking destinations. A new biography, "Deals Drama Drive: Michael Mon

entries.title: States sue HUD over a rule that would end housing aid for mixed-status families
entries.snippet: HUD defends the rule, saying it prevents illegal immigrants from exploiting eligibility requirements.

entries.title: Paxton drops Texas lawsuits that accused doctors of illegally providing transgender youth care
entries.snippet: May Lau and M. Brett Cooper were among three doctors who Paxton called "scofflaws" and "radical gender activists" in lawsuits that threatened to impose steep fines and revoke their medical licenses.

entries.title: U.S. jury finds Chinese tech giant Huawei guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud
entries.snippet: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries under U.S. sanctions and making false statements to officials.

entries.title: Pentagon sharply criticizes Canada over modernizing military
entries.snippet: The Defense Department accused Ottawa of failing to make the tough decisions needed to modernize its military and meet NATO commitments.

entries.title: Australia set to pass online safety laws with multibillion-dollar fines for tech giants
entries.snippet: The Australian government clinched a political deal on Tuesday to introduce online safety laws that could expose tech giants to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable online harms.

entries.title: Democrats supporting abortion rights won big in midterms, but vast changes unlikely soon
entries.snippet: States with bans will still have enough Republicans in power to likely block any repeal attempts for now.

entries.title: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton held by ICE after detention at D.C. airport
entries.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security says Xie overstayed her visa and did not have authorization to study in the U.S. Xie's lawyer says she has a pending asylum application.

entries.title: Experts say failed climate talks could worsen inequality, but progress not stalled
entries.snippet: Dozens of nations objected to the summit's final text because it didn't mention fossil fuels that drive climate change or increase financial help for poorer countries.

entries.title: West Coast king tides could break decades-old records and flood communities
entries.snippet: In the San Francisco Bay Area, tides could reach 2.6 feet above normal Tuesday before peaking Wednesday at 2.8 feet above normal, said Dial Hoang, a National Weather Service forecaster.

entries.title: Will wind ground your favorite balloon in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade?
entries.snippet: Local officials are wary of the balloons getting blown off course and into spectators. Macy's says it'll make the decision Thursday morning.

entries.title: Trump will give Medal of Freedom to Giuliani, a fierce political ally who led New York through 9/11
entries.snippet: As President Donald Trump's personal lawyer, he was a central figure in efforts to overturn Trump's 2020 presidential election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.

entries.title: Rep. Raskin expands investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s investment firm
entries.snippet: A top House Democrat is broadening his investigation into Donald Trump Jr.'s venture capital fund 1789 Capital by demanding records from four companies that secured an investment before benefiting from lucrative federal contracts or policies.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: European court finds states can turn back migrants in some cases
entries.snippet: Europe's top human rights court ruled that member states can turn back migrants unless they've been identified as people who were at risk of suffering.

entries.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy and Hungary's Magyar meet amid thaw in ties
entries.snippet: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar has arrived in Ukraine for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and ethnic Hungarians. Both leaders say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest.

entries.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

entries.title: HIV infections could rise amid aid cuts, UN warns
entries.snippet: The impact of United States government funding cuts has been dramatic for many HIV programs, UNAIDS warned. The agency expects that 2027 data to show an increase in new infections after being on the cusp of ending AIDS.

entries.title: Pope Francis diaries recount spiritual crisis, him seeing the 'Devil'
entries.snippet: Extracts of the late Pope Francis' diaries have been published, the first release of its kind since the 1960s. They discuss his struggles with his role in the Vatican and visions of the devil and the gates of hell.

entries.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
entries.snippet: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

entries.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
entries.snippet: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.

entries.title: Why Iran's medicine supply chain is failing
entries.snippet: Pharmacies in Iran are closing, hospital deliveries have stalled and patients are rationing doses or turning to black markets.

entries.title: Colombia: Car bomb attack injures at least 23
entries.snippet: The explosion in Villavicencio coincides with the tenth anniversary of a peace accord with FARC guerrillas, casting doubt on Colombia's peace process.

entries.title: Germany's Wadephul 'shocked' by Trump's Nvidia intervention
entries.snippet: The German foreign minister has criticized Donald Trump's interference in the chip-maker's economic activities. Jensen Huang was brought back after stepping down as Nvidia CEO amid multiple scandals.

entries.title: Land mine deaths reach five-year high, watchdog says
entries.snippet: Myanmar reported the highest annual land mine casualty toll, followed by Syria and Afghanistan, ICBL report says. Since 1999, nearly 50 thousand people were killed by land mines.

entries.title: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
entries.snippet: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.

entries.title: Five women killed every hour by family members or partners — UN report
entries.snippet: On average, 129 women or girls were killed every day in 2025 by someone in their close social circle, UN data showed.

entries.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
entries.snippet: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

entries.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
entries.snippet: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

entries.title: EU imposes import quotas for hybrid vehicles from China
entries.snippet: The EU is trying to protect its own car manufacturers from what it called "overcapacity" in China. Carmakers in the bloc, especially in Germany, have been lagging behind their Chinese rivals.

entries.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
entries.snippet: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

entries.title: Istanbul 'lion hunt' ends with no big cat found after all
entries.snippet: After a major search operation for a lion on the loose in Istanbul woodlands, Turkish authorities said "the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat."

entries.title: Pakistani astronaut to join Chinese space mission
entries.snippet: A Pakistani astronaut is set to become to the first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a payload specialist, will join the Shenzhou-24 mission when it launches on Wednesday.
